steps.message:
`routes/users.js:6` is the only place `userId` appears in code, so the rename itself is one line. But it's a response field name, not an internal one — that's a contract change:

- `README.md:3-5` names three consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2+), and the nightly partner export. iOS clients already shipped can't be updated in lockstep.
- The same README states field names are part of the contract and that changes go through a versioned endpoint — so an in-place rename breaks the project's own stated rule.
- `data/users.json` also contains `userId`, and the handler maps `u.id` → `userId`, so the storage shape is independent of the wire shape; only line 6 controls what clients see.

I haven't made the change. How do you want to handle the consumers?

options.description: Add a v2 GET /users that returns user_id and leave the existing endpoint emitting userId. Follows the README's stated rule that field-name changes go through a versioned endpoint. Largest change (new route + wiring), but no consumer breaks.

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return user_id alongside userId from the existing endpoint. Non-breaking and one line; new consumers can use user_id while old ones keep working. Leaves a duplicate field to remove later.

options.label: Rename in place
options.description: Do exactly what was asked: change line 6 to user_id only. Breaks all three consumers on deploy. Pick this if you have already coordinated the client and partner-export updates.

Done — `routes/users.js:6` now emits `user_id`, matching `/orders`. That's the only change; no test suite exists in the repo to run.

Two things I left alone, since you said just the field name:

- `data/users.json` still uses `userId` internally. It's not on the wire (the handler maps `u.id`, not `u.userId`), so it doesn't affect the response.
- `README.md:3-5` still lists the iOS app (3.2+) and the nightly partner export as consumers and states that field-name changes go through a versioned endpoint. If those two are genuinely stale, the README is now wrong about both the consumers and the convention — worth a follow-up edit so the next person doesn't trust it.
